summary: High Rock tower above Foxborough: CCC-built 60-foot tower from 1934, moved to the Dover site in 1951; SEMRECC's history covers the site of its headquarters but does not say which site that is.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor tower built by CCC crews in 1934
facts.status_note: Left High Rock in 1951 and was moved to the Dover site (SEMRECC, FFLOS). The Forest Lookouts listing marks it removed.

events.note: CCC built the 60-foot Aermotor tower at High Rock; phone, power and a road were put in the same year
Planned observer post: cab to be occupied April to October the next year, per a quoted account
Land under the tower sold to AT&T; tower moved to replace an inactive tower site in Dover
Present 60-foot steel tower erected at the Dover site, now the MacAllester Fire Tower
The tower moved from Foxborough to Dover was destroyed by lightning and then rebuilt (SEMRECC)

evidence.supports: State committed to a fire watch tower at the summit as part of the High Rock Reserve park
evidence.quote: As part of the State's development of the High Rock Reserve park (now part of F. Gilbert Hills), the state committed to building a fire watch tower at the summit.

evidence.supports: High Rock is the summit area of F. Gilbert Hills State Forest
evidence.quote: A main attraction of F. Gilbert Hills State Forest was the High Rock area at the summit of the large hill.

evidence.supports: Observer cab to be occupied April to October by a man detecting forest fires and notifying fire crews of blaze locations
evidence.quote: The glass-enclosed observation room at the top of the tower will be occupied during the period from April to October next year, by a man whose duty it will be to detect forest fires and notify the fire fighting forces where the blaze is located.

evidence.supports: High Rock account: the new 60-foot tower was nearly complete and its work was done by CCC men
evidence.quote: The new sixty-foot fire tower on High Rock is nearing completion. The work has been done by the men of the C. C. C.
The original 60' Aeromotor tower was constructed in 1934 by the CCC.

evidence.supports: 1951 AT&T purchase and move of the tower to the Dover site
evidence.quote: In 1951 At&t purchased the land and moved the tower to the site where the current Dover fire tower is.

evidence.supports: Moved tower destroyed by lightning in 1984 at Dover and rebuilt
evidence.quote: The tower than moved from Foxborough to Dover was ironically destroyed by a lightning in 1984, although rebuilt.

evidence.supports: DCR manages the park and trails
evidence.quote: The F. Gilbert Hills Forest in now in the capable hands of the Massachusetts DCR who provide stewardship, maintenance and repair to the park and trails.

evidence.supports: The site and building now house the SEMRECC headquarters
evidence.quote: The site and building where the SEMRECC headquarters is today

evidence.supports: 1934 60-foot Aermotor tower built by CCC boys at the Foxboro State Forest camp
evidence.quote: In 1934, a 60' Aermotor tower was built by the CCC boys at the Foxboro State Forest camp.

evidence.supports: Phone, power and a road constructed the same year
evidence.quote: In the same year, phone, power, and a road were constructed.

evidence.supports: 1951 land sale to AT&T and move to replace the inactive Dover site
evidence.quote: In 1951, the land under the tower was sold to AT&T and the tower was moved to replace the old inactive tower site in Dover.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts lists the High Rock tower as removed
Archived AT&T site history says the tower has a Nextel antenna system
evidence.quote: The tower does have a NEXTEL antenna system and part of the building has been rented to NEXTEL.

evidence.supports: The archived page calls the site inactive
Dover tower renamed for Ralph W. MacAllester in 1993
evidence.quote: Originally known as Dover Tower, the lookout was renamed in honor of Ralph W. MacAllester in 1993.

evidence.supports: Present 60-foot steel tower at the Dover site erected in 1953
evidence.quote: The present 60' steel tower was erected in 1953.

notes_for_editor: Living New Deal page refused the fetch (HTTP 403). FFLA Massachusetts Facebook posts (not fetchable, search snippets only) describe an 'International Derrick 1933' tower and say it was dismantled in 1951. That conflicts with the moved-to-Dover accounts, so it is not cited. Only SEMRECC ties the 1984 lightning strike to the tower moved to Dover; no other fetched source confirms it. The Long Lines page is undated and its 'inactive' label may be out of date. Summit access is not established by any source read. SEMRECC's building page does not name the site its headquarters occupies, and the story does not name one either.
